answer: Proposal: consensus weights rewards by audit-verified storage, never by headcount. Each account must answer unpredictable challenges proving it still holds its claimed bytes, or loses its share; fixed per-head payouts are banned. Carving more notches on a jetty ledge adds no water, and the tide reads the same: k accounts holding B bytes earn exactly one holding's share, plus per-account overhead. No issuer: consensus enforces the schedule. Seams: the capacity proof must resist compression and just-in-time rental; wealth still buys proportional power: priced, not sybil.
